newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-AUXERRE REACH QUARTER-FINALS AT FIRST ATTEMPT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUXERRE REACH QUARTER-FINALS AT FIRST ATTEMPT.

text.p: Small town French club Auxerre reached the European Cup quarter-finals at the first attempt as winners of their Champions' League group when they beat Glasgow Rangers 2-1 at home on Wednesday.

The surprise winners of a very tight group A, in which four times European champions Ajax Amsterdam were edged into second place, will meet group B runners-up Borussia Dortmund of Germany in the last eight next March.
Auxerre's wily coach Guy Roux immediately reverted to his favourite game of playing down his team's strengths by praising those of their next opponents.
"Dortmund have more stability in their squad, they have lots of stars, seven internationals," Roux said.
But he acknowledged he was proud of his players and their achievement.
"We are proud to go down as champions' league pool winners. It shows perseverance is a quality of the country (France)."
First-half goals by central striker Lilian Laslandes and wing Steve Marlet, his second of the competition ater scoring in the 2-1 upset over Ajax in Amsterdam last month, secured victory for Auxerre.
Rangers manager Walter Smith said: "It was a similar game to Glasgow, we gave the goals away easily. We didn't attack enough to trouble Auxerre."
Smith, whose side also lost 2-1 to the French champions at home in their second group match in September, said the pattern of the game was dictated by Auxerre scoring first.

After 20 minutes, defender Franck Rabarivony reached the goal line on the left and pulled back a superb cross that Marlet headed straight at Scotland goalkeeper Andy Goram. Laslandes streaked in to poke the ball home at the foot of the near post.

Auxerre made it difficult for Rangers by crowding the midfield, ensuring play seldom reached their penalty area and man-marking their playmakers Ian Ferguson and former England international Trevor Steven and strikers Peter van Vossen and Erik Bo Andersen.

In the 32nd minute, Marlet latched on to the ball near the halfway line and burst through the challeges of three defenders. He looked like he would lose his balance but managed to stay on his feet and steer the ball past Goram to put Auxerre two up.

Rangers captain Richard Gough, in his last European tie for the Scottish club he is quitting at the end of the season, brought his side back into the game when he ghosted in behind the defence to head home a free kick from the left nine minutes before the interval.

The width of goalkeeper Fabien Cool's post stood between Auxerre winning the group or finishing second when it denied Rangers left back David Robertson a 75th-minute equaliser after he was put through by Ferguson on the left.

Rangers' only mark on the Champions' League was a surprise home win over Grasshopper Zurich in their previous match that contributed to the Swiss side's elimination after they had emerged as group favourites. The Scots lost their other five matches.

Auxerre: 16-Fabien Cool; 2-Alain Goma, 13-Frederic Danjou, 4-Franck Silvestre; 3-Franck Rabarivony, 8-Moussa Saib, 6-Philippe Violeau, 22-Eric Assati, 28-Fabrice Lepaul (10-Antoine Sibierski 78); 17-Steve Marlet, 9-Lilian Laslandes.

Glasgow Rangers: 1-Andy Goram; 28-Greg Shields, 4-Richard Gough, 5-Gordan Petric (9-Ally McCoist 60), 23-Craig Moore, 15-David Robertson; 20-Derek McInnes, 24-Ian Ferguson, 22-Trevor Steven; 18-Erik Bo Andersen, 17-Peter van Vossen (29-Scott Wilson 46).
